## The DOM

### Project Overview

- repo link [here](https://github.com/firtman/coffeemasters-vanilla.git)
- The only reason for us to use local server is because of fetching a json which is not possible if we just open an HTML file ( index.html ) directly in browser.

```jsx
npx serve .
```

### Some Points to know for Sure ( Inspect VS Source Code )

- The elements tab in chrome shows the String representation of HTML.
- This given code is correct. But how can it be, it has no html tag, no body, head tags. Actually it is valid html → can be verified from the W3C validator. ( `title` tag is mandatory )

![Untitled](Untitled%20594.png)

- Because all those tags are optional in HTML specs.
- Now why does it work anyway ? html file and DOM are not same things. `head` and `body` are implicit for DOM ( which is structure in memory ). So html file we write is different from DOM we see in the `Elements` tab in `chrome`.

![Untitled](Untitled%20595.png)

- The `Inspect` tab is our parsed html code converted into DOM by the browser. The relationship exists between both but 100% of the times.

### How does browser know which elements go where ?

- Doctype and title are mandatory tags.
- We can have script, link tags in our html file.
- When the parser ( browser ) finds first `visible` element on html file it ends `head` tag and starts `body`.  In our case its `h1`, can be `p` .

![Untitled](Untitled%20596.png)

What if we have `p` before the `title` tag → it will be in body, wont do anything to html though 😃. 

### Scoping query selector ( Performance tips )

- `querySelector` picks the first element from the DOM, for instance

```jsx
document.querySelector("header") -> // gets the first header element from our html file.
```

- querySelectorAll() gets all such elements like

```jsx
document.querySelectorAll(".navlink"); // gets all navlinks
```

- querySelector make search whole document, which causes performance impact.
- So the more we narrow down the search span the better performance will be. As shown below

![Untitled](Untitled%20597.png)

- Its like caching the object for future use in our code.

### Adding Scripts async and defer

- In Vanilla JS we used to have a worry about declaring script tag each/per JavaScript file, which was tiresome.
- That is why previously we used bundler to bundle different javascript files in one Js file.
- Though in Modern JavaScript we do not need to create one script tag per JS file.

### Pattern

- One entry point file. Like `app.js`. The only one we are reffering.
- One root script `app.js` , while other script most probably web components, services etc will have their own folder ( An Opinion only for this usecase )

```jsx
<script src="app.js"></script>
```

- When Browser sees this line
    - Stops executing all other HTML until it downloads entire JS file, execute it and then moves on further.
    - That is why its advised ( used to ) to add script at bottom of body tag.
- We have better way now. When not sure which to use `defer` or `async` simply use `defer`. Browser downloads file when sees `script` tag though do not executes until `html` is parsed completely.
- `Async` is for use cases which are needed to be done immediately as web starts.
- It does not halt Parsing and browser starts downloading file in parallel and halts parsing when files is ready ( downloaded ), executes it and continues parsing the remaining html.

### Main Script Setup

- In some browsers even after the whole parsing is done, still DOM is being created.
- There is an event we can use to make sure everything ( DOM even ) is loaded before we start manipulating DOM because before this event if we try to manipulate maybe its not even there in DOM yet.

```jsx
window.addEventListener("DomContentLoaded",function manipulateIndexHtml(){
	let nav = document.querySelector("nav");
	consooe.log(nav);
})
```

- There is also an event `load` but how does it differ from `DomContentLoaded` .
- `load` waits for everything to finish like fonts, stylesheets, images, videos etc. Which grabs away the opportunity from us too manipulate DOM earlier

Some DOM events are specific to only few elements, like `DOMContentLoaded` and `popState` to only window object. They cannot be used with any other object.

![Untitled](Untitled%20598.png)

- For now we have only seen DomContentLoaded to now follow this naming pattern.

### Binding Function to events in DOM objects

![Untitled](Untitled%20599.png)

OnEvent properties 

![Untitled](Untitled%20600.png)

![Untitled](Untitled%20601.png)

- The problem is that since its an event only the latest one for a given single element will take effect as its just like getter and setters properties.
- Limited to a specific elemeent. While addEventListener covers as many elements as we can think of. Plus it can listen for more than one once. Like we can have DomContentLoaded with window multiple times and each will be fired.

### Advance Event Handling

- We can use an `object` containing certain properties as third argument to `addEventListener` for advance event handling like setting `once` to `true` allows to execute events only once

![Untitled](Untitled%20602.png)

- In very simplified terms `passive: true` means that hey browser you can passively execute my eventListener passively, do not wait for it to finish to do your work. In reality its much more complex.
- We can also remove event listeners `removeEventListener` . Its relevant only in case of Single page apps where we are adding and removing elements on page. But if a user is leaving a page wither through navigation or closing browser. We do not have to clean up JavaScript.
    - So used when injecting and removing elements. Allows us to clean functions in memory we do not want anymore.

### Dispatching our own events

- We can create our own events. These events can be called on any element like `button` or even `document` .

### Helpful Short-hands

[Initializing Project – You Don't Need that Library](https://firtman.github.io/vanilla/lessons/the-dom/initializing-project)

- There are many ways you can create your own short-hands in javascript by manipulating prototype for HTML element

```jsx
const $ = function(args){ return document.querySelector(args);}
const $$ = function(args){ return document.querySelectorAll(args);}

HTMLElement.prototype.on = function(a, b, c){ return this.addEventListener(a, b, c); }
HTMLElement.prototype.off = function(a, b){ return this.removeEventListener(a, b); }
HTMLElement.prototype.$ = function(s){ return this.querySelector(s); }
HTMLElement.prototype.$$ = function(s){ return this.querySelectorAll(s); }
```

### Initializing The Services

[Creating Initial Services – You Don't Need that Library](https://firtman.github.io/vanilla/lessons/the-dom/creating-initial-services)

- Not representing any phenomenon, its just a Design Pattern where we have an object or way through which we offer different services to the app.
- The name of `Store` file is Capital because we are gonna create a `singleton` object, in such cases we follow the `Class` syntax of starting Capital letter.
- We are gonna use ECMAScript by using exporting it as default object.
- By looking at simple JS file, we cannot tell if its a module or not. So `Store` variable will be local only to the `Store.js` file.
- For Now we cannot import API and Store in our app.js as for this we need app.js to be a module
- So just add `type = module` in the scrip tag for `app.js` in `index.html` .

```jsx
<script src="app.js" defer type="module"></script>
```

- This app loaded as module, so every variable that we define in JS is not gonna be Global variable for the whole page but just for that file. While this file can export and import things from other files.

### Global Context by default

- By default variables in all files in JS are global, this causes name conflicts even in between different files.
- But it can be avoided by `type = module` for script tag.

### Loading Menu Data

- By violating the module pattern for once we are gonna make store available globally. By attaching it with an object for `window`

```jsx
window.app = {};
app.store = Store;
```

Making Menu Data Fetching Modular 

```jsx

window.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", async () => {
	const menu = API.fetchMenu();
});
```

[Creating Menu Services – You Don't Need that Library](https://firtman.github.io/vanilla/lessons/the-dom/creating-menu-services)

- We can simply fetch data in DONContentLoaded event as shown. But its not modular. Lets us make it better
- Create a Menu.js file in `services` and export a function named loadData()

Note: Browsers need full path to files, vs code default import does not have `.js` at the end so make sure you have `import API from "./API.js";` and not `import API from "./API";`

- In Menu.js we are gonna declare the FetchMenu function and get data.

```
import API from "./API.js";

export async function loadData(){
	const menu = await API.fetchMenu();
}
```

Now back to `app.js` and call this `loadData` function there

```
window.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
	loadData();
});
```

Now start server ( `npx serve .` ) and go to console and just write app to see data inside menu object

## Routing

### Navigating between pages using DOM

- As usual when we are section 1 we see its section , click on section 2 and it gets displayed etc.

![Untitled](Untitled%20604.png)

DOM’s point of View 

![Untitled](Untitled%20605.png)

- Remove previous page and inject new page. Where page → is an abstract idea, a design pattern where it will be a DOM element which will render the contents of one particular section of our APP.

![Untitled](Untitled%20606.png)

- The other way is to have all pages there and just Hide and show them

![Untitled](Untitled%20607.png)

both have there pros and cons, like the later one may not be beneficial in a very large application 

### Router

- Typically these days changing the content of page based on what user selects is called as Router. Keep in mind that it is not part of DOM.
- Its just an abstract idea. There is no router in DOM, its something we will code using the DOM Apis.

![Untitled](Untitled%20608.png)

- We can make use of history api from DOM to push new entries to navigation history.
- When we see URL in the URL bar, we think its a response from a web server. This part of the statement suggests that when you enter a URL into the address bar of your web browser and press Enter, the browser sends a request to a web server, which then provides a response or content associated with that specific URL. In other words, the URL you see in the address bar typically corresponds to a specific resource or page on the web server.
- But in reality it may not be always the case, due to advancements in web technologies, the URL displayed in the address bar may not always directly correspond to a new request to the web server. This is primarily due to the use of client-side scripting languages like JavaScript.
- Also we can make changes in the URL or create fake URL which may not even exists on the server. JavaScript, when used in combination with the browser's history API, can manipulate the URL displayed in the address bar without necessarily making a new request to the web server. In essence, JavaScript can change the URL displayed to the user without actually loading a new page from the server. This is often done for creating smoother user experiences in web applications, such as single-page applications (SPAs) and dynamic web content.
- We can also listen for changes, like we can know the user using `back` button.

### History API

![Untitled](Untitled%20609.png)

- We can make of `pushState` to push a new url ( third argument ) to `pushState` method on history API.
- The first arg is for metadata maybe of an optional data. Will see in details
- 2nd arg is un-used so can be set as `null` .
- The popstate event is fired whenever there is a change in URL. Remember it does not change the content in DOM
- It will be on us to change the content in DOM after listening for changes in URL. This is what an idea of a `router` is.

### popstate

There’s a cath however in this case. 

![Untitled](Untitled%20610.png)

- This causes browser to enter a new navigation, out of our web app.

![Untitled](Untitled%20611.png)

- If you are creating an SPA ( Single Page Application ), configure your server properly. for the purpose what happens when user tries that fake URL or press refresh on a URL that is fake. Thhe server returns 404.
- Typically when using a SPA, we set up server so every request, every url should forward to index HTML, not redirect but forward.

### Making SPA Router from scratch

- Make a Router module and import in app.js

Router.js

```jsx
const Router = {
	init: function initialization(){
		return;
	},
	go: function goToThisRouter(route, addToHistory=true){
		console.log(`Going to ${route}`);
	}
}

export default Router;
```

app.js

```jsx
//rest of the code
window.app = {};
app.store = Store;
app.router = Router;
// rest of the code
```

### Note

- When we click on the coffee logo the browser makes request to server which we do not want to happen. We do not want our links (we want to manage)to go to server.
- means when we click on a link, will tell browser do not go this link we will do it, its like intercepting the navigation itself.

### Intercepting Navigation

- We can prevent default behavior of browser by using preventDefault(), method on the element, like an anchor element in our case.

```
const Router = {
	init: function initialization(){
		document.querySelectorAll("a.navlink").forEach(a => {
			a.addEventListener("click",event => {
				event.preventDefault();	// prevents the default behavior of browser 
				console.log("Link Clicked");
			})
		});
	},
	go: function goToThisRouter(route, addToHistory=true){
		console.log(`Going to ${route}`);
	}
}

export default Router;
```

 now we gonna initialize the router in the DOMContentLoaded event listener.

```jsx
window.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
	loadData();
	app.router.init(); 
});
```

![Untitled](Untitled%20612.png)

### href vs getAttribute

Note: The 

`href` property returns the full URL while the 

`getAttribute` method will only return the pathname if that's what's in the attribute.

- We can get `href` using anchor.href or anchor.getAttribute(). The difference is as stated above.

Another important thing is either to use `a` or event to get `href`

- We can use `a` because of closure. But we would use `event` as it refers to event targeted element which is a specific `anchor` element.

![Untitled](Untitled%20613.png)

- We also check url to make whatever the current pathname is we navigate it. Like /order

```
init: function initialization(){
		document.querySelectorAll("a.navlink").forEach(a => {
			a.addEventListener("click",event => {
				event.preventDefault();	// prevents the default behavior of browser 
				const url = event.target.getAttribute("href");
				Router.go(url);
			})
		});
		// check the initial url
		Router.go(location.pathname);
	},
```

### Adding to history

```jsx
go: function goToThisRouter(route, addToHistory=true){
		if(addToHistory){
			history.pushState({route},"",route);
		}
	}
```

- First argument to pushState is data: any ( it can be string, object, array etc )

![Untitled](Untitled%20614.png)

- Third argument is our URL which is a string for sure.

### Changing DOM Content

```jsx
go: (route, addToHistory = true) => {
    if (addToHistory) {
      history.pushState({ route }, "", route);
    }
	let pageElement = null;
	switch(route){
		case "":	
			pageElement = document.createElement("h1");
			pageElement.textContent = "Menu";
			break;
		case "/order":
			pageElement = document.createElement("h1");
			pageElement.textContent = "Your order";
			break;
	}

	document.querySelector("main").appendChild(pageElement);
  },
```

We are using switch to decide which route it is and then using technique of injecting and removing from DOM as we discussed previously.

The Problem 

- Since we are appending, the previous items stay thus we see repeated Menu and Your Order.

![Untitled](Untitled%20615.png)

Two solutions

### Quick and Dirty

```
document.querySelector("main").innerHTML = "";
document.querySelector("main").appendChild(pageElement);
```

### Better way

- Using children of the main we just call remove method on it.

> Note: Childnodes do also return text, empty spaces, newline characters. While children only return DOM elements.
> 
> 
> ![Untitled](Untitled%20616.png)
> 

for now we are using dirty method. 

```jsx
const cache = document.querySelector("main");
cache.innerHTML = "";
cache.appendChild(pageElement);
```

### Note

stay at top when navigating to other page.

```
window.scrollX = 0;
      window.scrollY = 0;
```

## Dynamic Routing

in Router.js

```
switch (route) {
      case "/":
        pageElement = document.createElement("h1");
        pageElement.textContent = "Menu";
        break;
      case "/order":
        pageElement = document.createElement("h1");
        pageElement.textContent = "Your order";
        break;
      default:
        if (route.startsWith("/product-")) {
          pageElement = document.createElement("h1");
          pageElement.textContent = "Details";
          const paramId = route.substring(route.lastIndexOf("-") + 1);
          pageElement.dataset.id = paramId;
        }
```

- Though we can use regular expressions but there is a simple way as well.
- The default case represents the dynamic product route, we make sure of it by having a check of `route` starting with `/product-` but it can be anything.

```
const paramId = route.substring(route.lastIndexOf("-") + 1);
pageElement.dataset.id = paramId;
```

The next part is to pass down this id to the DOM element. The better way is to make use of `data` attributes. Which is `dataset` property here.

- If we try to use back button url changes but not content, because we are not listening to URL changes.
- Lets move to router.js and inside init we are gonna use eventHandler for popState → fired every time based on a user interaction.
- The route under event → state can be accessed because we did set it using history.pushState in the go function before while we called pushState() method on history.

```
window.addEventListener("popstate",event => {
		Router.go(event.state.route, false);
	})
```

## Web Components

### Overview and Custom Elements

- Definition of what a web component is

![Screenshot 2023-10-24 at 10.03.14 AM.png](Screenshot_2023-10-24_at_10.03.14_AM.png)

- Mostly web components are user interfaces like we used to have in React.
    
    ![Screenshot 2023-10-24 at 10.06.21 AM.png](Screenshot_2023-10-24_at_10.06.21_AM.png)
    
- Web Components are modular, reusable building blocks for web development.
- They encapsulate related functionality and user interface elements.
- Web Components are similar in concept to components in UI libraries like React and Angular.
- They are custom HTML elements that can be created and used in web development.
- Web Components are compatible with modern browsers.
- They are based on a set of standards, including custom elements, HTML templates, and Shadow DOM.
- There is no single way to create Web Components; developers have the freedom to define and use them as they see fit, once they understand the underlying APIs.

### Creating Web Components

starting with these instructions

[Create the Custom Elements – You Don't Need that Library](https://firtman.github.io/vanilla/lessons/web-components/create-the-custom-elements)

- After creating a file in components folder like MenuPage.js, can we access this element in the index.html now ? If we write it in HTML, its only acting as unknown element in the DOM.
- To access it will have to link the element and the html ( index.html ) in our case.
- We can link it in App.js by importing them here ( export each in its own respective file )
- And by only importing it in JS which is loaded by browser, browser is gonna execute the module so that now its knows we are defining a new web components.
- Similar for Order and Details page and then import in App.js
- Now we can create an instance of these using createElement method in our Router.js file.

[Update the Router Copy – You Don't Need that Library](https://firtman.github.io/vanilla/lessons/web-components/update-the-router%20copy)

```jsx
switch (route) {
      case "/":
        pageElement = document.createElement("menu-page");
        pageElement.textContent = "Menu";
        break;
      case "/order":
        pageElement = document.createElement("order-page");
        pageElement.textContent = "Your order";
        break;
      default:
        if (route.startsWith("/product-")) {
          pageElement = document.createElement("details-page");
          pageElement.textContent = "Details";
          const paramId = route.substring(route.lastIndexOf("-") + 1);
          pageElement.dataset.id = paramId;
        }
    }
```

### Loading Templates

- In index.html, we have many templates like meny-page, details-page etc.

[Use the Templates – You Don't Need that Library](https://firtman.github.io/vanilla/lessons/web-components/use-the-templates)

- Next is to load these templates into our custom elements.

First we try to do it in Constructor for our custom element i.e `DetailsPage.js`

- Say for instance we take `menu-page-template` and after referring it, we clone it ( because the templates are not useable themselves ).

```jsx
const template = document.getElementById("menu-page-template");
const content = template.content.cloneNode(true);
this.appendChild(content);
```

- cloneNode() is provided with `true` value because we want deep cloning ( cloning nested elements as well ).
- But in doing so inside constructor, its causes error because while constructing an element we cannot return anything or have children of it.
- Instead it should be done inside `connectedCallback()` .

```jsx
 		
	connectedCallback() {
    const template = document.getElementById("menu-page-template");
    const content = template.content.cloneNode(true);
    this.appendChild(content);
	}
```

Now we can go to our [localhost](http://localhost) running server, we can see that

### Testing

- In the current state if we try to use any styles for our template they be applied on global levels which is not what we want.
- To solve that comes `Shadow DOM` into the picture.

### Applying a Shadow DOM

- We do this inside the constructor,
- using `this` context of the class we call attachShadow() with `mode` set to `open` meaning outside DOM can interact with this inside DOM if needed.

```
export class MenuPage extends HTMLElement {
  constructor() {
    super();
    this.root = this.attachShadow({ mode: "open" });
  }
  // when the component is attached to the DOM
  connectedCallback() {
    const template = document.getElementById("menu-page-template");
    const content = template.content.cloneNode(true);
    this.root.appendChild(content);
  }
}

customElements.define("menu-page", MenuPage);
```

as here in the code

- We are appending the content to shadowDOM now, so that its styles are local to custom elements and not globally accessible unlike before.
- We can do all the template referencing and appending stuff back in constructor now, as now we are not adding children to yourself but in another document i.e shadowDOM.

## Reactive Programming with Proxies

### Creating a proxy

- Proxy is an event listener for data in the simplest terms possible.
    
    ![Screenshot 2023-10-31 at 11.01.58 AM.png](Screenshot_2023-10-31_at_11.01.58_AM.png)
    
- Proxy usage example.
    
    ![Screenshot 2023-10-31 at 11.19.05 AM.png](Screenshot_2023-10-31_at_11.19.05_AM.png)
    
    - Once the proxy is set, then original object is not used anymore, as in this example.
    - Proxy has some special functions like get, called when we try to access a property from the proxy.
        
        ![Screenshot 2023-10-31 at 11.15.38 AM.png](Screenshot_2023-10-31_at_11.15.38_AM.png)
        
    - This shows how we can validate properties being assigned values, using the `set` function.
    
    ![Screenshot 2023-10-31 at 12.02.29 PM.png](Screenshot_2023-10-31_at_12.02.29_PM.png)
    

### Proxy Handler and Traps

![Screenshot 2023-10-31 at 12.04.30 PM.png](Screenshot_2023-10-31_at_12.04.30_PM.png)

- While Trap is simply a method on a Proxy handler like the `get` and `set` in our previous example.

![Screenshot 2023-10-31 at 12.08.06 PM.png](Screenshot_2023-10-31_at_12.08.06_PM.png)

Example of Proxy Trap methods. 

![Screenshot 2023-10-31 at 12.08.32 PM.png](Screenshot_2023-10-31_at_12.08.32_PM.png)

### Implementing the Proxy

- In our Store.js we implement a proxy, where if a store property is modified like the menu or cart etc then we dispatch a custom event.

```jsx
const Store = {
  menu: null, // means not have it yet or still loading
  cart: [],
};

const ProxyStore = new Proxy(Store, {
  set(target, property, value) {
    target[property] = value;
    if (property === "menu") {
      window.dispatchEvent(new Event("appmenuchange"));
    }
    if (property === "cart") {
      window.dispatchEvent(new Event("appcartchange"));
    }
    return true;
  },
});

export default ProxyStore;
```

- The event is dispatched using window and not document ( because of shadow DOM ) as we have two document now while only one window for whole app.

### Rendering the Menu

```jsx
export class MenuPage extends HTMLElement {
  constructor() {
    super();
    this.root = this.attachShadow({ mode: "open" });
    const styles = document.createElement("style");
    this.root.appendChild(styles);
    async function loadCSS() {
      const request = await fetch("/components/MenuPage.css");
      const css = await request.text();
      styles.textContent = css;
    }
    loadCSS();
  }
  // when the component is attached to the DOM
  connectedCallback() {
    const template = document.getElementById("menu-page-template");
    const content = template.content.cloneNode(true);
    this.root.appendChild(content);
    window.addEventListener("appmenuchange", () => {
      this.render();
    });
  }

  render() {
    if (app.store.menu) {
      this.root.querySelector("#menu").innerHTML = "";
      for (let category of app.store.menu) {
        const liCategory = document.createElement("li");
        liCategory.innerHTML = `
				<h3>${category.name}</h3>
				<ul className="category"></ul>
			`;
        this.root.querySelector("#menu").appendChild(liCategory);

        category.products.forEach((product) => {
          const item = document.createElement("product-item");
          item.dataset.product = JSON.stringify(product);
          liCategory.querySelector("ul").appendChild(item);
        });
      }
    } else {
      this.root.querySelector("#menu").innerHTML = "Loading....";
    }
  }
}

customElements.define("menu-page", MenuPage);
```

- Added a new method render to render the menu when we have received the menu items array of objects from the fetch request.
- When it does the `appmenuchange` event triggers.

- beside every other thing ( we have already seen )

| target | currentTarget |
| --- | --- |
| [event.target](http://event.target) denotes the lower level element interacted with | Denotes the current element interacted with  |
| The button is target, as its inside the wrapper anchor for which we have click event, so if we click button it has two events click on button and click on anchor wrapper as well. | Like anchor tag in this code is currentTarget as event is being listened for this whole wrapper ( anchor ) |

import { getProductById } from '../services/Menu.js';

export default class DetailsPage extends HTMLElement {

    constructor() {
        super();

        this.root = this.attachShadow({ mode: "open" });

        const template = document.getElementById("details-page-template");

}

### Order Page

- First of all we make a new service named Order.js.
- Then we first get the product using its id.

```
import {getProductById} from './Menu'
export async function addToCart(id) {
	const product = await getProductById(id);
	
}
```

- After that we have to check if this item already exists in the cart or its a new entry.

```
const results = app.store.cart.filter(
    (prodInCart) => prodInCart.product.id == id
  );
```

- Now we can check if result is an empty array ( new entry in cart ) or have some value ( already exist ).

```jsx
if (results.length == 1) {
  // product already in the cart
  // update current Item
} else {
  app.store.cart.push({ product, quantity: 1 });
}
```

- In else condition we are pushing the object into the cart but this is wrong in terms of how our proxy is setup.
- When we are pushing something into cart are we changing it ? no so it will not trigger the change event. Because pushing is like changing the content of carts but not the Cart itself.
- So instead of mutating the array itself we are just gonna create a new array and place existing data in it and mutate it with new data. Now assign it to the old cart.
- In this manner, the change event triggers.

  

```jsx
app.store.cart = [...app.store.cart, { product, quantity: 1 }];
```

Final code

```jsx
import { getProductById } from "./Menu";
export async function addToCart(id) {
  const product = await getProductById(id);
  const results = app.store.cart.filter(
    (prodInCart) => prodInCart.product.id == id
  );
  if (results.length == 1) {
    // product already in the cart
    // update current Item
    pp.store.cart = app.store.cart.map((p) =>
      p.product.id == id ? { ...p, quantity: p.quantity + 1 } : p
    );
  } else {
    app.store.cart = [...app.store.cart, { product, quantity: 1 }];
  }
}

export function removeFromCart(id) {
  app.store.cart = app.store.cart.filter((p) => p.product.id != id);
}
```

In the ProductItem.js we previously had a un-implemented section so here we call addToCart function and add item to cart.  

```
this.querySelector("a").addEventListener("click", (event) => {
      console.log(event.target.tagName);
      if (event.target.tagName.toLowerCase() == "button") {
        addToCart(product.id);
      } else {
        app.router.go(`/product-${product.id}`);
      }
      event.preventDefault();
    });
```

How to know if there is something in cart without visiting orders page. 

in App.js we add an event listener `appcartchange` and set the bade value and color for this purpose. 

```jsx
window.addEventListener("appcartchange", event => {
	const badge = document.getElementById("badge");
	const qty = app.store.cart
})
```

here for quantity its not simply length because it may return 1 for 10 cappuccino which is not true.

to get around this we will count quantity value and not the length of cart.

 

```
window.addEventListener("appcartchange", (event) => {
  const badge = document.getElementById("badge");
  const qty = app.store.cart.reduce((acc, item) =>
    acc + item.quantity, 0);
  badge.textContent = qty;
  badge.hidden = qty === 0;
});
```

### Displaying items in the Cart

[Finishing the Cart – You Don't Need that Library](https://firtman.github.io/vanilla/lessons/reactive-programming/finishing-the-cart)

- We are not gonna use shadowDOM for the CartItem, becuase we want to share the document with whole page instead of creating a new one.
- **This also signifies the fact that ShadowDOM is not always to be used or used everywhere.**
- It shares its CSS with its container.

### Why is that we always have to import every new component ( custom element aka web component ) in app.js ?

- Its because the browser does only add the custom element in its dom like Car Item in our case.
- But the custom element itself is gonna be empty and not contain anything at all, so for browser to know if its has something it will go and search for its class in the web component or custom elements.
- For registering the custom element is to use **Define** as we do in the in each custom element by calling these lines at end of those custom elements we make.

```jsx
customElements.define("cart-item", CartItem);
```

- Importing these custom elements only triggers when the App.js runs in overall JS execution, so these files run and let browser know that these custom elements does have a content which needs to be rendered.

## Binding Form Data

- Now we are trying to bind data with forms so they are more reactive to changes made in any input or object at large.
1. Creating private object in OrderPage.js.

```
#user = {
		name: "",
		phone: "",
		email: ""
	  }
```

1. Then we gonna make a function named setFormBindings().
    1. DOM provides us a way to access all the collection of elements of a form like inputs, TextArea, buttons, radioButtons etc.
    2. But in actual we cannot directly access the form in the OrderPage using `window` object ? why is that 
        1. Its is because its inside a shadow DOM which is not accessible from outer/global dom.
        
        ```jsx
        setFormBindings(form){
        	// Set Double Data binding
        	this.#user = new Proxy(this.#user, {
        		set(target, property, value){
        			target[property] = value;
        			form.elements[property].value = value;
        		}
        
        	})
          }
        ```
        
    3. The form element is an `HTMLFormControlCollections` which cannot have forEach ( way-around is there ).
    4. This ultimately completes to two way binding or Double Binding.
    
    ### Infinite Loop Problem for Double Data Binding
    
    When we are changing form both ways using proxy and change event. The `change` event in DOM only triggers when the user changes it in the browser and it does not trigger when changes are being made from JS as in Proxy. 
    
    ### How and Where to use it
    
    - First we use it at end of render because until the form in shadowDOM would’ve been declared so we can use it.
    - Why at end ? because the form is not in Global DOM other wise we could access it wherever dom is available.
    
    ![Screenshot 2023-11-15 at 3.08.42 PM.png](Screenshot_2023-11-15_at_3.08.42_PM.png)
    
    ### How to check if it even works or not
    
    - Let us check it using some events trigger to make our lives easier.
    
    ```jsx
    form.addEventListener("submit",event => {
    		event.preventDefault();
    		alert(`Thanks for your order ${this.#user.name}`);
    		// clearing form
    		this.#user.name = "";
    		this.#user.email = "";
    		this.#user.phone = "";
    	})
    ```
    
    We did two things here
    
    1. First started listening for `submit` but why submit we could have listened for click as we are gonna check if when we click on button it should be trigger ? isn’t it. 
        1. No actually not, we want to make sure every case covers, a smartphone user may not click button but just press `submit` on virtual keyboard in Iphone/Android.
    2. We are clearing form using simple assigning of empty strings. 
        
        ![Screenshot 2023-11-15 at 3.18.35 PM.png](Screenshot_2023-11-15_at_3.18.35_PM.png)
        
        - Why? becuase it expects that set returns true when a value is assigned which we did not.
        
        ```jsx
        setFormBindings(form) {
            // Testing for form submit events
            form.addEventListener("submit", (event) => {
              event.preventDefault();
              alert(`Thanks for your order ${this.#user.name}`);
              // clearing form
              this.#user.name = "";
              this.#user.email = "";
              this.#user.phone = "";
            });
            // Set Double Data binding
            this.#user = new Proxy(this.#user, {
              set(target, property, value) {
                target[property] = value;
                form.elements[property].value = value;
                return true;
              },
            });
            Array.from(form.elements).forEach((element) => {
              element.addEventListener("change", (event) => {
                this.#user[element.name] = element.value;
              });
            });
          }
        ```
        
    
    ### Issue: When we go back to the Menu we see nothing
    
    **Cause** 
    
    - in MenuPage.js we call connected callback only when there is a change in the app menu ( when the page loads and fetches data ) any other time this event never triggers causing issue such as what we saw now.
    
    **Remedy**
    
    ```jsx
    connectedCallback() {
        const template = document.getElementById("menu-page-template");
        const content = template.content.cloneNode(true);
        this.root.appendChild(content);
        window.addEventListener("appmenuchange", () => {
          this.render();
        });
        this.render();
      }
    ```
    
    Call when you page loads initally without under any event listener.
